rows.observation: A vertical baler stands in the recycling bay. The ram guard door carries a captive-key interlock and the door is closed. After Thursday's ram seal replacement the fitter signed the plant back on line; the sheet records the seal change but carries no interlock test result. The bay floor is swept.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state the interlock's protective behaviour after the seal replacement
owedFact.branchA: established: the ram guard door interlock's protective function was verified after the seal replacement and before the baler was returned to service
owedFact.branchB: not established: the ram guard door interlock's protective function was verified after the seal replacement and before the baler was returned to service

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the ram guard door interlock's protective function
decisionDivergence.ifB: the baler must be taken out of service until the ram guard door interlock's protective function is verified

owedFact.evidenceSpan: the sheet records the seal change but carries no interlock test result

firstPassClarifications.question: Was the ram guard door interlock functionally tested — confirmed to stop the ram when the door is opened — after the seal replacement and before the baler was put back on line?

conjuncts: the interlock's protective function was verified after the seal replacement and before return to service
rows.designIntent: The existing question names the function, excludes mere presence, and carries the temporal bound. v3.1 should rely on it, keep the fact unresolved, and not replace it.

rows.observation: A fitter is about to break a flanged joint on a steam header in the boiler house. The boiler is off and the header isolation valve is padlocked shut; a second fitter witnessed the isolation. He opened the header drain and left it open, and the header pressure gauge sits behind the lagging and has not been read since. The walkway grating is secure.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state the header's current pressure
owedFact.branchA: established: the residual pressure in the steam header has been released and confirmed at zero before the flanged joint is broken
owedFact.branchB: not established: the residual pressure in the steam header has been released and confirmed at zero before the flanged joint is broken

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about residual pressure in the steam header
decisionDivergence.ifB: the flanged joint must not be broken until the header is confirmed at zero

owedFact.evidenceSpan: the header pressure gauge sits behind the lagging and has not been read since

firstPassClarifications.question: Has the header pressure been read at the gauge and confirmed at zero before the joint is broken, rather than relying on the drain having been opened?

conjuncts: the residual pressure has been released and confirmed at zero before the joint is broken
rows.designIntent: The existing question names the confirmation act and excludes the adjacent evidence (the drain having been opened) by name. v3.1 should rely on it.

rows.observation: A gas-fired paint oven runs on the finishing line. The over-temperature cut-out sits inside the control cabinet and cannot be seen from the floor. At the annual service the engineer filed a certificate listing a thermocouple change and a fan-belt swap; it records no over-temperature trip test. Dust has settled on the cabinet top.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the over-temperature cut-out was trip-tested
owedFact.branchA: established: the over-temperature cut-out has been verified to shut off the gas when the setpoint is exceeded
owedFact.branchB: not established: the over-temperature cut-out has been verified to shut off the gas when the setpoint is exceeded

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the over-temperature cut-out's protective function
decisionDivergence.ifB: the oven must be shut down until the over-temperature cut-out's protective function is verified

owedFact.evidenceSpan: it records no over-temperature trip test

firstPassClarifications.question: Was the over-temperature cut-out trip-tested at the annual service — confirmed to shut off the gas when the setpoint is exceeded — even though the certificate does not record it?

conjuncts: the cut-out has been verified to shut off the gas when the setpoint is exceeded
rows.designIntent: An unobservable control with a sufficient existing question. Tests that the new adjacent-property boundary does not disturb the unseen-control heuristic that already works.

rows.observation: A fitter is about to change a damaged belt scraper at the tail drum of a quarry conveyor. He has locked the drive isolator with his own padlock. The belt runs over a gravity take-up tower that holds tension on the belt when the drive is off, and the take-up release log carries no entry for today. The tail drum guard has been set aside.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the gravity take-up tension has been released and confirmed at zero
owedFact.branchA: established: the conveyor drive is isolated AND the gravity take-up tension has been released and confirmed at zero before work at the tail drum
owedFact.branchB: not established: the conveyor drive is isolated AND the gravity take-up tension has been released and confirmed at zero before work at the tail drum

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about drive isolation and stored take-up tension at the tail drum
decisionDivergence.ifB: work at the tail drum must not start until the drive is isolated and the take-up tension is released and confirmed at zero

owedFact.evidenceSpan: the take-up release log carries no entry for today

firstPassClarifications.question: Was the conveyor drive isolator locked off before work started at the tail drum?

conjuncts: the gravity take-up tension is released and confirmed at zero
rows.designIntent: A AND B, and the existing question reaches only A. A truthful yes is available to someone who locked the isolator and never touched the take-up. v3.1 should find the question insufficient and supply or request what actually establishes the second conjunct.

rows.observation: An operator is opening a cartridge filter on a chemical dosing skid. The upstream supply valve is closed and padlocked and a tag hangs from it. The line flush record for this morning is signed. The skid's local pressure indicator sits behind the frame and has not been read. A drip tray is in place under the housing.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state the line's current pressure
owedFact.branchA: established: the dosing line is isolated AND flushed AND confirmed at zero pressure before the filter housing is opened
owedFact.branchB: not established: the dosing line is isolated AND flushed AND confirmed at zero pressure before the filter housing is opened

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the dosing line's state before the filter housing is opened
decisionDivergence.ifB: the filter housing must not be opened until the line is confirmed at zero pressure as well as isolated and flushed

owedFact.evidenceSpan: The skid's local pressure indicator sits behind the frame and has not been read

firstPassClarifications.question: Was the upstream supply valve locked closed and the line flushed before the filter housing was opened?

conjuncts: the dosing line is confirmed at zero pressure
rows.designIntent: A AND B AND C, and the existing question reaches A and B. The harder case: two of three conjuncts covered, so a verifier reading topic-level would call it sufficient.

rows.observation: Two sprayers are working inside a spray booth on the paint line. The booth's low-airflow alarm panel shows a green lamp at the door. The alarm's trip point was set at commissioning three years ago, and this year's verification sheet for the alarm has not been completed. The booth doors close on their own.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the low-airflow alarm will actually trip at its set point
owedFact.branchA: established: the booth's low-airflow alarm has been verified to trip at its set point and is currently operable
owedFact.branchB: not established: the booth's low-airflow alarm has been verified to trip at its set point and is currently operable

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the low-airflow alarm's trip function
decisionDivergence.ifB: spraying must stop until the low-airflow alarm's trip function is verified

owedFact.evidenceSpan: this year's verification sheet for the alarm has not been completed

conjuncts: the low-airflow alarm has been verified to trip at its set point and is currently operable
rows.designIntent: A green lamp shows the panel is powered, not that the alarm will trip. Nothing was asked. v3.1 should propose a question reaching the trip function.

rows.observation: A pedestal grinder stands in the fitting shop and a fitter is dressing a bracket on it. The wheel guard is bolted on and the work rest is in place. This morning's shop checklist is initialled; it covers housekeeping and lighting. The work rest gap was last set at the wheel change six weeks ago. No tools lie on the machine.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state the current gap between the work rest and the wheel
owedFact.branchA: established: the work rest gap is currently set within the safe clearance for the wheel in use
owedFact.branchB: not established: the work rest gap is currently set within the safe clearance for the wheel in use

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the current work rest gap
decisionDivergence.ifB: the grinder must be taken out of use until the work rest gap is confirmed within the safe clearance

owedFact.evidenceSpan: The work rest gap was last set at the wheel change six weeks ago

conjuncts: the work rest gap is currently within the safe clearance for the wheel in use
rows.designIntent: The strongest adjacent trap in the cohort: guard bolted on, rest "in place", a signed checklist covering OTHER items, no tools, and a historical setting. None of them is the current gap. Structurally analogous to HR-04 without reusing its wording.

rows.observation: A contractor is working near the south edge of a flat roof plant area, where there is no permanent guardrail. He is clipped to a temporary line rigged to a roof anchor. The anchor carries an ID tag. The roof access log is signed for today, and the permanent guardrail along the north edge was inspected at the annual survey. The anchor's load-test record is held in the site office.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state when the anchor was last load-tested or whether that test is current
owedFact.branchA: established: the roof anchor carrying the temporary line has a current valid load test
owedFact.branchB: not established: the roof anchor carrying the temporary line has a current valid load test

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the anchor's load test
decisionDivergence.ifB: work at the south edge must stop until the anchor's load test is confirmed current

owedFact.evidenceSpan: The anchor's load-test record is held in the site office

conjuncts: the anchor has a current valid load test
rows.designIntent: An ID tag is identification, not testing; the signed access log and the inspected guardrail belong to a DIFFERENT edge and a different control. The trap is that the row reads well-managed.

rows.observation: A fitter is clearing a jam inside the shrink-wrap tunnel on a packaging line. He has locked off the line's main control panel, applied his own lock and proved that panel dead. The tunnel's heater bank is fed from a separate distribution board on the far wall, and the log at that board carries no entry for today. The line's guard doors are open.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the heater bank's own supply has been isolated
owedFact.branchA: established: the shrink tunnel heater bank's separate supply has been isolated before work inside the tunnel
owedFact.branchB: not established: the shrink tunnel heater bank's separate supply has been isolated before work inside the tunnel

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the heater bank's separate supply
decisionDivergence.ifB: work inside the tunnel must stop until the heater bank's separate supply is isolated

owedFact.evidenceSpan: the log at that board carries no entry for today

conjuncts: the heater bank's separate supply has been isolated before work inside the tunnel
rows.designIntent: Related-control trap: a thorough, correct isolation of the MAIN panel, and a separate source untouched. Tests "a control on one source says nothing about a separate one" as a proposal opportunity rather than as a sufficiency question.

rows.observation: A welder works at a bench with a movable local exhaust ventilation hood. The thorough examination report for the LEV system is on the wall and is in date; it covers the fan and the ductwork. The hood at this bench has been repositioned since that examination, and no capture check has been recorded at the new position. The bench is tidy.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the hood captures fume effectively at its current position
owedFact.branchA: established: the LEV hood captures welding fume effectively at its current position
owedFact.branchB: not established: the LEV hood captures welding fume effectively at its current position

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about capture at the hood's current position
decisionDivergence.ifB: welding at this bench must stop until the hood's capture is confirmed effective at its current position

owedFact.evidenceSpan: no capture check has been recorded at the new position

conjuncts: the hood captures fume effectively at its current position
rows.designIntent: An in-date examination whose STATED SCOPE is the fan and the ductwork, and an owed property outside that scope. Tests "an inspection settles only what it is stated to cover".

rows.observation: A workshop air receiver supplies the shop ring main and the compressor runs on load. The written scheme examination certificate is on the wall and is in date. An automatic drain was fitted at the last examination. The receiver's safety valve was function-tested at that examination two years ago and there is no later test record.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state whether the safety valve currently lifts at its set pressure
owedFact.branchA: established: the receiver's safety valve currently lifts at its set pressure
owedFact.branchB: not established: the receiver's safety valve currently lifts at its set pressure

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the safety valve's current lifting pressure
decisionDivergence.ifB: the receiver must be taken off load until the safety valve is confirmed to lift at its set pressure

owedFact.evidenceSpan: there is no later test record

conjuncts: the safety valve currently lifts at its set pressure
rows.designIntent: Historical-versus-current trap, wrapped in an in-date certificate. A test two years ago is evidence about then. Tests "a check made at some earlier time tells you about then, not about now".

rows.observation: Before the annual internal inspection of a workshop air receiver the fitter isolated the compressor and locked the isolator with his own lock. He opened the manual blowdown, watched the receiver gauge fall to zero and remain there for two minutes, and a second fitter witnessed the gauge reading zero. The inspection hatch is still bolted.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: no confirmation of the receiver's pressure state was recorded
owedFact.branchA: established: the receiver has been vented and confirmed at zero before the inspection hatch is opened
owedFact.branchB: not established: the receiver has been vented and confirmed at zero before the inspection hatch is opened

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about the receiver's pressure
decisionDivergence.ifB: the inspection hatch must not be opened until the receiver is confirmed at zero

owedFact.evidenceSpan: watched the receiver gauge fall to zero and remain there for two minutes

conjuncts: the receiver has been vented and confirmed at zero before the hatch is opened
rows.designIntent: The observation SETTLES the supplied fact: gauge watched to zero, held two minutes, witnessed. The supplied whyUnresolved is the raising as a first pass would have written it, and the text contradicts it. v3.1 should not invent a gap; challenging the fact as already settled is the defensible outcome.

rows.observation: A forklift operates in a warehouse aisle. Pedestrian walkways are marked on both sides and a physical barrier separates the walkway from the aisle for its full length. A banksman stands at the aisle entrance. The truck's amber beacon is working. The floor was swept at the start of shift.

owedFact.whyUnresolved: the observation does not state how often pedestrians cross the aisle during a shift
owedFact.branchA: established: the number of pedestrian crossings of the aisle per shift is known
owedFact.branchB: not established: the number of pedestrian crossings of the aisle per shift is known

decisionDivergence.ifA: no additional control is required on account of uncertainty about pedestrian crossing frequency
decisionDivergence.ifB: additional segregation must be installed until the pedestrian crossing frequency is known

owedFact.evidenceSpan: a physical barrier separates the walkway from the aisle for its full length

conjuncts: the pedestrian crossing frequency is known
rows.designIntent: A MAGNITUDE question whose governing control — full-length physical segregation plus a banksman — is stated present, so both answers lead to the same thing being done today. Challenging the fact, or declining a clarification, is defensible; inventing a stop-work gap is not.
